title: Credit committee
transcript:
Joshua Gordon: Okay, let's get started. It's 11:00 on September 1st. We have two individual credits on the agenda today, both Cassandra's, plus a quick pipeline and process item at the end. Cassandra, do you want to lead with {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0211}}?
Cassandra Hampton: Sure. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0211}} has been with us since June 2024, checking is a_00439 and the existing loan sits on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00440}}. They're asking for a restructure and a step-up in the facility, roughly $85,000 additional on top of the current balance. Internal risk rating is medium.
Joshua Gordon: What's driving the ask?
Cassandra Hampton: Home renovation and consolidating two outside revolving lines. Payment history on our loan has been clean, no lates in the last 14 months. Checking balances have been a bit lumpier since spring, though.
Jasmine Johnson: I ran the numbers last week. Debt service coverage on the pro forma comes in at 1.28x, which is under our 1.35x policy floor for medium-risk individuals. If we count the consolidation of the outside lines it improves, but only to about 1.33x.
Joshua Gordon: So still short even with the consolidation.
Jasmine Johnson: Yes, by a hair. The other thing is the income documentation. Two of the three most recent pay statements are in the file, but the third is missing and the self-employment income piece is only supported by a one-page summary.
Heidi Davis: That's a gap. We can't take a one-page summary as support. We need the tax returns or at least a signed 4506-type transcript request.
Cassandra Hampton: Agreed. I can get those from the client. I spoke with {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0211}} on Friday and they were open to providing whatever we need. I have the contact details in ClientHub, phone {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0211}}, and I'll follow up by email at {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0211}} so there's a paper trail.
Brendan Alvarez: Do we know whether the outside revolving lines will actually be closed after payoff? If they stay open the consolidation benefit is mostly illusory.
Cassandra Hampton: Good point. I'd make closure of those lines, or at least a zero balance with a freeze letter, a condition of funding.
Joshua Gordon: I'd rather see actual closure. Brandon, can the closing process handle verification of closure?
Brandon George: Yes, we can pay off direct to the creditors and require a closure confirmation letter before we release the final disbursement. It adds a few days but it's clean.
Lynn Chase: From a relationship standpoint, is there a risk we lose them if we make this too tight?
Cassandra Hampton: Some. They have an outside offer they've mentioned but didn't specify. I think they'd accept a slightly lower amount over losing the deal.
Joshua Gordon: Let's think about a counter. If we cut the increase to $65,000, what does DSCR do, Jasmine?
Jasmine Johnson: At $65,000 with the consolidation I get about 1.38x. That clears policy.
Joshua Gordon: Then that's my proposal. Approve at $65,000 additional, subject to full income documentation, closure of the two outside lines at payoff, and an updated rating review in six months. Any objection?
Heidi Davis: No objection, as long as documentation is complete before the approval letter goes out. Conditional approval only.
Brendan Alvarez: Fine with me.
Joshua Gordon: Okay, conditionally approved at $65,000. Cassandra owns collecting the income docs by September 11th. Brandon owns the payoff and closure-letter process once docs are in.
Brandon George: Got it.
Joshua Gordon: Next, {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0116}}. Low risk, client since March 2024. Cassandra?
Cassandra Hampton: This is a renewal and modest rate adjustment. Loan is {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00245}}, checking is a_00244. Balance has been paid down to about 62% of original. Never a late payment. They've asked for a rate reduction of 50 basis points.
Heidi Davis: Do they have a debit card tied to a_00244? I saw a card reference in the file.
Cassandra Hampton: Yes, that's the card on the checking account, {{CARD_NUMBER:a_00244}}. It came up because they reported a fraud dispute on it in July. It's resolved and credited back.
Jasmine Johnson: I saw that. The dispute doesn't affect credit performance. Scoring is unchanged and the model has them in the top tier.
Lynn Chase: Is a 50 basis point cut within pricing guidelines for low risk?
Joshua Gordon: Within the retention band, yes, up to 75 basis points with committee sign-off. Given the payment history I'm comfortable with 50.
Brendan Alvarez: Any reason not to approve?
Heidi Davis: Only that the rate sheet was updated in August, so we need to make sure the new rate references the current index, not the old one.
Cassandra Hampton: I'll confirm with Brandon on the document template.
Brandon George: The template was refreshed Aug 24th. I'll double check that the margin language matches.
Joshua Gordon: Then approved, 50 basis point reduction, effective the next payment cycle. Brandon prepares the amendment, Cassandra sends it to the client for signature.
Cassandra Hampton: Will do. I'll send it by end of day Thursday.
Joshua Gordon: Last item, pipeline. Lynn, anything flagged?
Lynn Chase: Two files are aging past 30 days in LoanOrigination waiting on KYC clearance. I'll post the details in the lending channel after this. I'd like us to escalate through the KYC pipeline channel if they sit another week.
Joshua Gordon: Please do. Let's also commit to a standing check on aging files every Tuesday. Lynn, you own that list.
Lynn Chase: Fine.
Joshua Gordon: To recap. One, c_0211 conditionally approved at $65,000, documents due September 11th, Cassandra. Two, payoff and closure verification, Brandon. Three, c_0116 rate cut approved, amendment from Brandon, delivery by Cassandra Thursday. Four, aging file list and escalation, Lynn. Thanks everyone.
